topics.topic: Email-verified mark initial value and lifecycle
questions: What value does the mark have when an administrator creates a pending staff account, and can any event clear or otherwise change it after it is set?
What value does the mark have when an administrator creates a pending staff account, before activation?
What value does the mark have when an ordinary staff account is created, and can any later event clear or otherwise change it?

quotes:
The hash-free `StaffAccountView` of the new account, `pending_verification`
with `email_verified` false.

- **Lifecycle:** `pending_verification → active ↔ suspended → disabled`
  (disabled terminal), with one second entry: the first administrator of
  R0-07 is created directly `active` with `email_verified_at` set and
  `created_by = None`. `pending_verification` means awaiting the
  administrator's activation; no email is verified (R0-23). An account
  authenticates only in `active` status; `email_verified_at` decides no
  access. Suspension and disabling invalidate active sessions; no
  notification is sent (R0-23).

- **Created/modified by:** an administrator creates the account (in
  `pending_verification`, with the initial password of R0-19), changes its
  status — activation `pending_verification → active` sets
  `email_verified_at` (R0-19) — and replaces its email by the recovery
  override, the only email change (R0-20, R0-23). The holder changes only
  their own `password_hash`, by presenting the current password; that change
  revokes the holder's other sessions and keeps the one it is made through.
  `role` is set at creation and never changes: no operation changes a role.
judgement.why: The later model and public operation specify false at ordinary account creation, set the mark on activation and recovery, preserve it through suspension or reinstatement, and define no clearing operation.

questions: Which concrete operation returns this mark, and which principal types or capabilities are allowed to observe it?
Which principal may obtain this account view, through what product action, and what failure is returned to principals that may not view it?
Which concrete account-reading operation shows the mark, and which principal types are allowed to receive that output?

topics.topic: Sole-administrator host-level credential recovery contract and trust boundary
questions: Who is trusted to perform this recovery, what concrete host-level action and inputs recover the administrator, what state may it change, and what observable success and failure outcomes does it have?

What named host actor and operation perform this recovery, what inputs and stored facts may they change, what observable success and failure outcomes exist, and where is the host/product trust boundary?

What host-level action exists for a sole administrator who has lost both password and login email, including its actor, authority, inputs, stored changes, observable success, failures and audit treatment?

quotes:
No product operation recovers a sole administrator who has lost both password
and email: the bootstrap command of R0-07 refuses once any staff account
exists, and such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product
(owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions
delegated).

A staff member who has lost the password has no recovery inside the product:
the password changes only through its holder presenting the current one, and
an administrator may disable that account and create a new one (R0-14,
R0-19); a sole administrator's loss stays the host-level operation of R0-20.
judgement.divergence: One implementation provides a branchable host command that changes the existing administrator's email and password while preserving its identity; another requires direct SQLite repair or creates a replacement administrator, which the host operator and recovered administrator notice through different results, identity, and audit history.
judgement.why: The text promises a host-level recovery boundary but names neither its authorized actor and action nor its inputs, permitted state changes, success, failures, or audit treatment.

witness.initial: Exactly one administrator account exists, and its holder has lost both the login email and password, so the first-administrator bootstrap refuses.
events: The deployment host operator attempts the host-level recovery mentioned by R0-20.
The administrator attempts to sign in using the recovery result.
outcomes: A defined host operation updates the existing administrator's credentials and reports a branchable success or failure.
The deployment instead requires direct storage repair or creation of a different administrator, producing different identity and audit consequences.
witness.observer: The host operator and the recovered administrator
basis:
No product operation recovers a sole administrator who has lost both password
and email: the bootstrap command of R0-07 refuses once any staff account
exists, and such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product
(owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions
delegated).

The host operator
runs a local administrative command that creates exactly one active
administrator when no staff account exists, and is refused once any exists.

questions: How can the replacement account be created when the disabled account still owns the mandatory unique normalized login email?
Can the replacement account use the disabled account’s email, and if so, what releases or transfers that unique identifier?

quotes:
Access-management failures; `IdentityInputRejected` for an invalid or taken
email or a password outside A16, before any insert.
Every implementation of StaffAccessRepository MUST insert exactly account and reject duplicate staff_id or normalized email.
`module:staff_identity`. Replace a staff member's login email by administrator recovery.

The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the `staff_id`
and the replacement email.

R0-20 (administrator-only, the one email change, A10), A16 for the
replacement, A13 (enhanced `staff.recovery_override` audit in the same
transaction).
judgement.why: The later contract rejects creation while the disabled account still owns the normalized email; an administrator must first replace that account's email through the recovery override before reusing the former address.

topics.topic: Actions exempt from the authenticated-portal-principal requirement
questions: Which actions are excluded from R0-23’s assertion that every actor is an authenticated portal principal?

quotes:
The principals,
staff roles, staff login and logout, staff administration, viewers, producers
and the first-administrator command are unchanged; whoever acts on the portal
does so as one of the three principal types through its own authentication.

The common authorization rule binds project-scoped operations. Without a
session the portal answers only: staff login, viewer entry with an access
link, and the liveness and readiness checks (R0-11).
judgement.divergence: The universal assertion requires every portal caller, including a health caller, to be one of the three authenticated principal types, while R0-15 permits unauthenticated liveness and readiness callers; the monitoring system notices whether its request succeeds.
judgement.why: R0-23 universally requires an authenticated portal principal, whereas R0-15 expressly permits public health actions without a session.

witness.initial: The service is running and able to answer health requests.
events: An unauthenticated monitoring system requests the liveness check.
outcomes: The request is refused because the monitoring system is not one of the three principal types acting through its own authentication.
The service returns the unauthenticated liveness answer permitted by R0-15 and R0-11.
basis:
The service answers an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check that
changes no product state and discloses no path, credential, schema, dependency
version, configuration or exception (Factory `21658368`,
`rules.http_transport_policy.health`).

The common authorization rule binds project-scoped operations. Without a
session the portal answers only: staff login, viewer entry with an access
link, and the liveness and readiness checks (R0-11).

topics.topic: Whether the no-message rule includes ordinary API and binary responses
questions: Does “any other message” prohibit only outbound notification and delivery channels, or does it also include ordinary HTTP API responses and authenticated binary responses sent to staff and clients?

quotes:
Client Portal is a backend service with an HTTP JSON API that gives a
renovation client a transparent read-only view of their renovation projects —
planned budget, actual expenses with documents, expense allocation, work
progress, completed work value, received payments, and progress photos — while
authorized staff manage the portal-owned facts behind that view.

Application resources and commands use JSON. The only non-JSON response is an
authenticated binary download for an already-authorized ExpenseDocument or
ProgressPhoto. The portal streams that object through its own boundary; it
never exposes `file_ref`, a filesystem path, storage credentials, or a
provider URL to the client.
judgement.why: The product explicitly promises HTTP JSON responses and authenticated binary responses, so the no-message rule concerns outbound messaging and does not prohibit request-response traffic.
